source: No measured rotation axis. A rotation period of 33.70 ± 0.31 days is measured (McQuillan et al. 2013, adopted by Torres et al. 2015), but with no axis it is not drawn: no spin is propagated. The display axis is celestial north at the catalogue position, placed in the plane of the sky; computed by skyPlaneOrientation in @cssearth/astronomy.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the display axis: the sky-north direction at the star, in the plane of the sky. +X is the display meridian, set so that grid longitude 0 faces the Sun and Earth at the scene epoch; east longitude. No spin is propagated.
qualification: Display convention, not a measurement. The rotation axis, spin sense and prime meridian of Kepler-186 are unmeasured, and its measured period is not drawn; the axis shown is where celestial north lies on the sky.
